thread:
Taylor Nguyen: tagging this thread for the new Acme pilot. scope: document search + two tool calls (create_invoice, update_invoice). Sales wants an SOW + acceptance criteria + ballpark for committed pricing at ~10k q/day. Demo requested in 10 business days.

Ravi Singh: propose success criteria split by flow: search path: precision@5 >= 0.80 and avg search p95 < 500ms; tool path: end-to-end tool-call success >= 95% (schema + side-effect verification); cost: avg token cost per query <= $0.0035 for hosted or provide reserved commit options; security: SSO+SCIM & BYOK required before production.

Clara M.: model-fit thoughts: docs are long -> start with 16k context model as middle ground. Run parallel 32k smoke to verify recall on long contracts. Pipeline: embeddings index (HNSW) -> ANN top100 -> lightweight neural reranker/top prompt-based rerank -> generator formats tool payloads. If latency/cost too high, fallback: chunking + 8k model.

Priya Patel: timeline realistic: Days 0-2 ingest + canonical prompt collection (we need 50 labeled prompts from Acme), Days 3-6 embedding + index + recall checks, Days 7-8 reranker tuning & prompt templates, Day9 tool integration + E2E smoke, Day10 demo. send SOW draft by EOD.

Taylor Nguyen: add success criteria for privacy: PII redaction enabled for results with 99% recall on redaction tests and manual review showing no major leaks across 50 test prompts. Also require audit logging for tool calls and user actions.

Ravi Singh: embedding sizing: customer estimates ~220k docs, avg 2.5KB -> ~550M tokens. Start with 768-d embeddings; if recall low move to 1024-d. Recommend nightly incremental refresh; customer asked for near-real-time for invoices -> propose webhook-triggered immediate embedding for critical docs.

Clara M.: reranker options: lightweight learned reranker (quantized 8-bit) or prompt-based contrastive scoring. For the POC go prompt-rerank first (fast to iterate) then swap to small reranker if needed. We'll capture precision/latency delta.

Priya Patel: pricing ask: finance needs the usage profile to propose commit tiers. Example calc: 10k q/day ~ 300k q/mo. provide hosted estimate and reserved commit (monthly) with lower per-query unit. @Finance will you review? :money_with_wings:

Taylor Nguyen: infra checklist: service account & scoped keys, KMS permission for BYOK, SSO test account access, and logging forwarding. InfraBot create ticket.

InfraBot: ACME-POC-2124805555 created, infra ticket INF-8922 opened, service account provisioned, KMS onboarding pending customer auth.

Ravi Singh: sample curl for POC engineer (sem search + rerank):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/semsearch -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query":"How do I dispute an invoice charge?","top_k":100,"rerank":true,"model":"rwd-16k-search"}'
```

Clara M.: metrics to collect during POC: precision@1/5, recall@10, avg tokens per query, token cost per query, p95 latency for search and generation, tool-call success rate, PII redaction FP/FN. We'll include instrumentation hooks in the SOW.

Priya Patel: SOW items: timeline, labelled prompt set (50), acceptance criteria, fallback plan (chunking + 8k), canary rollout plan, rollback criteria (quality regression >5% drop in precision@5), and security deliverables (SCIM, BYOK, audit logs). I'll draft tonight.

Taylor Nguyen: blockers to surface on sales call: 1) security questionnaire/SSO creds, 2) finance commit pricing signoff, 3) customer providing 50 test prompts, 4) validate 16k model latency on their sample docs.

Ravi Singh: extra tech note: test quantized variant of the generator for cost reduction if token-cost target not met. Also precompute embeddings for high-frequency docs to reduce runtime cost.

Clara M.: agree. we'll run A/B: prompt-rerank vs learned reranker and capture quality & cost. Also ensure schema validator for create/update invoice tool calls (no malformed payloads).

Taylor Nguyen: thanks team. next check-in Thu 9:30am PT. Priya, ping when SOW ready; Ravi/Clara please add short runbook for the POC engineer. :rocket:
